papers.title: CABrain: A Correlation-Aware Brain Foundation Model for EEG Decoding
papers.summary: Introduces CABrain, an EEG foundation model that replaces purely random masked-patch pretraining with GCN-based conditional positional encoding to model inter-channel correlations plus an adaptive masking strategy that modulates reconstruction difficulty. Across ten benchmark datasets, these components individually and jointly achieved state-of-the-art or competitive EEG decoding performance.

papers.title: Chronic neuropeptide S treatment improves sleep architecture and reduces Aβ-related pathology in APP/PS1 mice.
papers.summary: Tested 14-day intracerebroventricular neuropeptide S (1 nmol/day) in APP/PS1 mice and found increased NREM sleep, reduced wakefulness, and lower Aβ-related pathology, with NPSR protein reduced in hypothalamus and hippocampus versus wild-type. BV2 cell experiments implicated ERK signaling and autophagy-related processes (LC3B-II, p62) in NPS-associated Aβ handling.

papers.title: Automated intracranial spike analysis across sleep-wake states localizes the seizure onset zone in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Applied Persyst automated sleep staging and intracranial interictal epileptiform discharge detection to 48-72 h recordings from 17 EPILEPSIAE and 10 pediatric patients, using an amplitude- and channel-consistency IED activity metric with logistic regression to localize the seizure onset zone. IED activity was higher in SOZ channels in every sleep-wake state, with N2 yielding the highest AUROC (0.69 EPILEPSIAE; 0.77 ACH).

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence
papers.summary: Validated the Dreem3 wearable EEG headband in 100 typically developing youth (9-26 years) over 3-4 consecutive nights of at-home recording against established age trends in sleep physiology. It replicated increases in NREM stage 2% and decreases in N3%, time in bed, and NREM delta and theta power with age, while some expected associations (total sleep time, sleep efficiency) did not reach significance though effect directions were largely as expected.

papers.title: Macroscale dynamics of EEG microstates constitute the periodic and aperiodic features of the neural power spectrum
papers.summary: Used orthogonal subspace projection to remove spatial projections of distinct EEG microstate configurations from high-density scalp and modeled cortical recordings, testing whether microstate dynamics generate periodic and aperiodic spectral features. Removing these projections strongly attenuated alpha and theta rhythms and the aperiodic 1/f background, and microstate duration and temporal persistence correlated with alpha power, theta power, and 1/f background.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment during adolescence ameliorates anxiety-related corticosterone, enhances memory, and is associated with changes in regional dopamine levels in the Wistar Kyoto rat, a putative model of endogenous depression.
papers.summary: In male and female Wistar Kyoto rats, adolescent environmental enrichment enhanced recognition and spatial memory, reduced serum corticosterone, and increased prefrontal, caudate putamen, and nucleus accumbens dopamine in a sex- and age-dependent manner. Correlational analyses linked recognition memory to prefrontal and striatal dopamine and anxiety to corticosterone and prefrontal serotonin.

papers.title: A Breathable Nanomesh-Textile Electrode Interface for Integrated Multimodal Monitoring.
papers.summary: The authors developed a duo-electrode wearable interface separating skin contact (electrospun nanomesh tattoo electrode) from electronic interconnection (compressible conductive taffeta-foam fabric electrode), integrated into a bodysuit and eyemask for multimodal ECG, EMG, EOG, and body-position monitoring. The system maintained reliable signal acquisition under motion and muscle activation, with performance comparable to or better than commercial hydrogel electrodes.

papers.title: Hypothalamic astrocytes fine-tune the signals governing metabolism.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that hypothalamic astrocytes are fundamental physiological regulators of energy homeostasis, in addition to their roles in high-fat-diet-induced hypothalamic inflammation and glucose intolerance. It discusses astrocyte heterogeneity, circadian and neuroendocrine interactions including puberty, and their potential as therapeutic targets including in responses to obesity drugs.

papers.title: Time of day metabolism and endocrine regulation of immune health.
papers.summary: This review proposes a chronodynamic model of immune health in which immune resilience depends on synchronization among central circadian clocks, food-entrainable metabolic oscillators, and peripheral cellular clocks. It argues that lifestyle-driven circadian desynchrony contributes to low-grade inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and immune aging, and proposes chrono-biomarkers for functional assessment of immune resilience.

papers.title: LBSNet: Lightweight Brain State Modeling via Learnable Spectral Prototypes for EEG-Based Fatigue Detection
papers.summary: The authors propose LBSNet, a lightweight EEG fatigue-detection network that encodes multi-band spectral structure and matches it to learnable spectral prototypes, which jointly determine temporal weights for aggregation. In subject-independent experiments on SEED-VIG and SADT, LBSNet outperformed seven baselines at low computational cost, and learned prototypes showed gradual redistribution of cross-band spectral states with increasing fatigue.

papers.title: The Cost of Control in Cardiometabolic Prevention: Insights from Sleep and Circadian Disruption.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses the costs of behavioral rigidity and self-monitoring in cardiometabolic prevention, drawing on insights from sleep and circadian disruption.

papers.title: Time-dependent efficacy of vitamin D3 against chronic stress-induced behavioral and circadian deficits via the hepatic VDR-clock axis.
papers.summary: Tested time-dependent vitamin D3 administration in a mouse chronic unpredictable mild stress model, giving VitD3 in the morning versus evening. Evening administration more effectively improved anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, hippocampal integrity, TNF-α, sleep duration, and serotonin synthesis, and more effectively restored hepatic Vdr rhythmic oscillation, with C. elegans validation supporting a VDR-circadian clock axis.

papers.title: Evening amber-lensed glasses in combination with a prescribed wake time advance circadian timing in adolescents with delayed sleep-wake phase disorder.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 36 adolescents with delayed sleep-wake phase disorder, wearing amber-lensed glasses in the evening plus a prescribed wake time advanced dim light melatonin onset by 40 minutes compared to a 29-minute delay in controls (p = .01), while sleep onset remained stable and weekend wake times were earlier in the treatment group, reducing social jetlag.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm and cancer-related pain: a systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 39 studies (35 human, 4 preclinical) found heterogeneous clinical evidence for temporal variation in cancer-related pain and analgesic requirements, with chronotherapy suggesting potential reductions in treatment-related neuropathy; mechanistic evidence was largely hypothesis-generating and methodological quality was limited.

papers.title: Cortical depth EEG-fMRI at 7T: Experimental setup and analysis pipeline to elucidate generating mechanisms of alpha oscillations.
papers.summary: The authors established a 7T EEG-fMRI laminar imaging and analysis pipeline with deveining to study alpha oscillation generators in 10 participants; negative alpha-BOLD correlations after deveining were significantly weaker in middle cortical depths than in superficial and deep depths, consistent with feedback/top-down processing.

papers.title: Circadian Clock Coordination of the Notch-to-Wnt Signaling Switch Promotes Regenerative Myogenesis
papers.summary: Using genetic and pharmacological approaches, this study identifies the circadian clock as a regulator of the Notch-to-Wnt signaling switch that promotes muscle stem cell expansion and myogenic differentiation during regeneration; clock activation enhanced regenerative myogenesis in dystrophic mouse and human myoblasts.

papers.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
papers.summary: Under a pre-specified, locked evaluation of scalp EEG seizure warning in 21 children, a statistical-process-control method detected 44% of seizures at 0.48 false alarms per hour (not better than random, p=0.86); a redesigned state-conditioned scheme detected 33% in cross-validation but failed external validation (19% vs 26% chance, p=0.96), indicating no robust above-chance warning.

papers.title: Serial Amplitude-Integrated Electroencephalography and the Burdjalov Score in Preterm Infants: A Prospective Longitudinal Bedside Study in the Neonatal Care Unit.
papers.summary: In a prospective longitudinal study of 48 preterm infants (125 aEEG recordings) and 29 term newborns, serial Burdjalov-scored amplitude-integrated EEG showed excellent interobserver agreement (ICC 0.98) and scores rose continuously with corrected gestational age, approaching maximal values around 37 weeks and matching term references; time to maturity did not differ by gestational-age stratum.

papers.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis and Sleep Disturbances: A Narrative Review of Bidirectional Mechanisms.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes clinical and mechanistic evidence for a bidirectional relationship between rheumatoid arthritis and sleep disturbances, implicating peripheral-to-central inflammatory signaling, circadian disruption, HPA-axis dysfunction, autonomic hyperarousal, and central sensitization. The authors note that most evidence is cross-sectional or from small treatment studies, so causality remains uncertain, and recommend distinguishing specific sleep disorders from nonspecific symptoms and combining RA management with disorder-specific sleep treatment.

papers.title: A sex-specific modification of the SARA questionnaire for obstructive sleep apnea screening: Comparative validation against six other tools in the HypnoLaus cohort.
papers.summary: Using the HypnoLaus population cohort (n=1540), seven OSA screening tools were validated against polysomnographic AHI≥15; NoSAS and updated SARA had the highest AUCs (0.741 and 0.693), and adding menopausal status improved SARA discrimination in women (AUC 0.675 vs 0.627), while anthropometry-weighted tools performed poorly in younger, lean women.

papers.title: Multimodal EEG-fNIRS complexity analysis can reveal the neurovascular coupling change with aging.
papers.summary: Simultaneous EEG-fNIRS with nonlinear entropy analysis in 20 young and 20 older adults across four cognitive tasks revealed task-specific age-related differences in neural and hemodynamic complexity and in cross-modal entropy measures, suggesting neurovascular coupling changes with aging reflect dynamic reorganization rather than uniform enhancement or impairment.

papers.title: Multiscale EEG network alterations in adolescents with depressive symptoms: static-dynamic connectivity, topological features, and exploratory scalp-level network hubs.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG from 96 adolescents with depressive symptoms and 154 controls was analyzed with adaptive-threshold multiscale networks, revealing theta-band static hyperconnectivity along midline prefrontal-central connections, reduced dynamic transition flexibility in prefrontal systems, and topological vulnerability of right prefrontal nodes (Fp2, F4), with overlap to exploratory neuromodulation hub projections.

papers.title: Intermittent hypoxia-driven gut microbial and metabolic remodeling in obstructive sleep apnea: mechanisms and evidence across target organs.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that intermittent hypoxia in obstructive sleep apnea remodels the gut environment—impairing epithelial barrier function and altering short-chain fatty acid, bile acid, and trimethylamine N-oxide pathways—and concludes the microbiota is a context-dependent amplifier of target-organ injury rather than a universal mediator, with human evidence remaining observational.

papers.title: Accelerometry-Derived REM Sleep Behavior Disorder Score Is Associated with Incident Parkinson's Disease in the UK Biobank
papers.summary: Applying a validated machine learning RBD classifier to 7-day wrist accelerometry in 87,975 UK Biobank participants followed for 10 years, the highest RBD-risk stratum (>99th percentile) showed an approximately fivefold increased hazard of incident Parkinson's disease with a dose-dependent relationship. The association was independent of PD polygenic risk score and synergistic with genetic risk, with high specificity (99.2%) supporting accelerometry for prodromal PD risk enrichment.

papers.title: Sex-related clinical profiles in obstructive sleep apnea: An integrated clinical, sleep study, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy analysis.
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of 767 patients undergoing drug-induced sleep endoscopy, women with OSA were older with more insomnia and mood disorders and greater improvement with jaw thrust (30.2% vs 18.4%), whereas men had higher BMI, obstruction at all airway levels, and more frequent surgical recommendations. The findings suggest an anatomy-driven pattern in men and a more functionally modulated profile in women.

papers.title: Evidence of high rates of burnout symptoms in a cohort with cluster headache.
papers.summary: In a Swedish cohort of 373 cluster headache patients, 65.9% of those in active bout had high burnout scores (>3.75 on Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire) versus 37.5% in remission (OR=3.22, 95% CI 1.93-5.38). High burnout was also associated with female sex and sleep deprivation as an attack trigger, and scores decreased with longer remission duration.

papers.title: MACS: mild by definition, challenging by nature.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence that mild autonomous cortisol secretion, though lacking overt Cushing phenotype, is associated with multisystem complications including cardiometabolic, skeletal, muscular, neuropsychiatric, and frailty-related consequences, and discusses diagnostic limitations of the 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test and individualized management including selective adrenalectomy.

papers.title: Habitual sleep duration and spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a prospective UK Biobank cohort study with supporting hospital-based neurosurgical data.
papers.summary: In a prospective UK Biobank cohort of 314,236 participants (1,387 incident spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhages), both short and long habitual sleep were associated with higher sICH risk, with stronger associations for long sleep (adjusted HR 1.55), supported by a hospital-based case-control analysis and U-shaped dose-response. Inflammatory markers neither explained nor reliably modified these associations.

papers.title: Side-to-side and other complex head movements as ictal signs in epilepsy: A video-EEG case series and review of literature.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: In a retrospective video-EEG series of 17 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy (631 seizures, 201 with complex head movements), ictal side-to-side and other complex head movements occurred across heterogeneous epileptogenic zones and lacked localizing or lateralizing value, likely reflecting seizure propagation.

papers.title: The Relationship of Triglyceride/Glucose Index with Disease Severity, Sleep, and Cognitive Functions in Patients with Geriatric Depression: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study with Healthy Controls.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 76 drug-naïve older adults with major depression and 40 controls, the triglyceride/glucose index (TyG) was significantly higher in depressed patients and independently associated with depression status (adjusted OR ~24.9), correlating with depression severity but not with cognitive function or insomnia severity. A TyG cutoff >8.78 showed 63.16% sensitivity and 95.00% specificity for depression.

papers.title: Restorative free time and psychological distress among employed family caregivers of individuals with cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 210 employed family caregivers of individuals with cognitive impairment, caregivers with less than 1 h/day of restorative free time and those sleeping less than 6 h/day had a significantly higher prevalence of psychological distress (Kessler 6), whereas working hours and caregiving duration were not significantly associated after adjustment. Limited restorative free time is proposed as a potential marker of psychological distress, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

papers.title: Differences in pulse oximetry saturation from sea level to high altitude among subjects with and without respiratory disease. A population-based, cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In the population-based PREPOCOL II study comparing 1146 adults with respiratory disease to 4613 controls across Colombian altitudes (18–3030 m), SpO2 was lower in those with respiratory disease at all altitudes and declined with increasing altitude and age in both groups; altitude showed the strongest association (standardized β −0.69 to −0.71), and the between-group difference emerged at approximately 1,500 m. SpO2 should be interpreted with reference to altitude and age.

papers.title: Circadian syndrome and headache accompanied by stomach pain among middle-aged and older Chinese adults: associations and the mediating role of frailty.
papers.journal: The journal of headache and pain
papers.summary: In CHARLS data (9,342 cross-sectional; 5,895 longitudinal), circadian syndrome was associated with higher odds of prevalent headache accompanied by stomach pain (OR 1.38) and increased incident risk (HR 1.33), with frailty mediating 19.72% of the longitudinal association.

papers.title: Quantifying Academic Risk Factors for Student Depression Using WHO Frameworks: Odds Ratios, SHAP Explainability, and Tipping Point Analysis
papers.summary: Using data from 27,880 Indian university students and an interpretability-focused approach (logistic regression odds ratios, Random Forest/XGBoost importance, SHAP values, tipping point analysis), the study found academic pressure to be the dominant depression risk factor (OR = 2.271; RF importance = 0.481), while study satisfaction (OR = 0.796) and sleep duration (OR = 0.835) were protective; ensemble models reached ~77–78% accuracy and AUC 0.845.

papers.title: Effect of neurofeedback-assisted mindfulness training on migraine severity, associated disability, sleep quality, and emotional distress: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized, parallel-group controlled trial of 66 adults with medium-to-high-frequency episodic migraine (5–14 monthly migraine days) testing a 12-week home-based neurofeedback-assisted mindfulness training program (Muse EEG headband, 60 sessions) plus standard care versus standard care alone, with monthly migraine days as the primary outcome and secondary outcomes including MIDAS, HIT-6, actigraphy/PSQI sleep measures, quality of life, and mood.

papers.title: Associations between the duration of outdoor sunlight exposure and the risk of developing 134 different diseases.
papers.summary: In a UK Biobank cohort of 281,282 participants followed a median of over 13.4 years, outdoor sunlight exposure duration was associated with 36 of 134 diseases after FDR correction: higher exposure with increased risks of malignant melanoma (HR = 1.052), obesity (1.039), cerebrovascular disease (1.028), and osteoarthritis (1.042), and lower risks of osteoporosis (0.975) and mineral metabolism disorders (0.968), with 30 diseases including depression, anxiety, and sleep disorders showing U-shaped associations.

papers.title: Health Information Literacy Moderates the Associations of Perceived Social Support with Insomnia and Infertility Psychological Distress in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technology: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1007 women undergoing assisted reproductive technology found perceived social support negatively associated with infertility psychological distress, with a significant indirect association through insomnia; health information literacy moderated the associations among social support, insomnia, and distress. These findings suggest psychosocial assessment should jointly consider social support, sleep problems, and health information literacy.

papers.title: Avermectin poisoning with panic-like symptoms: a case series.
papers.summary: A case series of two men with avermectin poisoning reports toxic effects including respiratory failure, hypotension, acidosis, coma, and delirium after oral ingestion, and local swelling with panic-like symptoms after intramuscular injection. In the oral case, panic-like symptoms were identified on psychiatric evaluation and improved with specialized treatment.

papers.title: From driving (L0) to living (L5): Intergenerational car comfort concept by Etic-emic theory.
papers.summary: Using a scoping review, trend analysis of 1789 Scopus articles (1953–2025), expert interviews, and group brainstorming, this study developed an Etic-Emic framework of intergenerational vehicle comfort, yielding 44 parameters classified as stable across automation levels (e.g., safety, vibration control, fuel efficiency) or emerging specifically at L5 (e.g., confidence to sleep or recline, legal liability transparency, cybersecurity). The resulting "Intergenerational Car Comfort" concept and Etic-Emic matrix is proposed as an actionable decision tool for OEMs on legacy architectures and new interior/HMI solutions.

papers.title: Effects of opioid-free intraoperative anesthesia versus opioid-based anesthesia on postoperative immune function in elderly patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty: a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In this single-center randomized controlled trial of 60 elderly patients undergoing unilateral total knee arthroplasty, intraoperative esketamine-based opioid-free anesthesia produced a significantly smaller postoperative decline in NK-cell proportion than opioid-based anesthesia (Δ = -5.51% ± 4.89% vs. Δ = -10.12% ± 5.39%; P < 0.001), along with better early analgesia, fewer PCIA demands, improved PSQI sleep scores, lower vasoactive and opioid consumption, and better short-term functional exercise capacity. CD8⁺ T cell and B cell proportions, extubation time, length of stay, rescue analgesia rate, and PONV incidence did not differ significantly.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
